WP4 deliverable 1 is a runner build PLUS a ledger-adoption operation - two tasks, not one.' Plan section 12 step 3 permits exactly this shape: 'receipt-adopt the exact production fingerprint into a namespaced Timeline ledger. Never replay the consolidated baseline.'

migrations.risk: high if replayed, zero if adopted. Every statement is a CREATE, so against a populated database this file fails loudly rather than corrupting quietly - but a partial application would leave the schema half-built. The runner refuses it on any database that already has application objects, which is why the risk that matters is procedural rather than structural: an operator reaching for drizzle-kit push instead of this path is the real hazard, and it is the hazard the runner exists to remove.
migrations.rollbackPlan: Fresh databases only: drop the database file (local) or the branch (CI). There is no in-place rollback for a baseline, and none is needed - a baseline is only ever applied where there was nothing before. For production the rollback is 'do not run this at all'; the adoption path writes one metadata row and nothing else, and its rollback is DELETE FROM signal_timeline_schema_migrations WHERE id = '0000_timeline_baseline'.
